00335.title: Imatinib for gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST): treatment and checks
00335.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00335.setting: KIT-positive gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST): unresectable/metastatic treatment or adjuvant treatment after resection
00335.summary: The usual National Cancer Control Programme starting dose is 400 mg by mouth every day with food. For progression in advanced disease, a specialist may consider 800 mg daily as 400 mg twice daily. Adjuvant treatment after resection is described as up to 3 years in this National Cancer Control Programme document; your specialist confirms duration using current risk and evidence. The 28-day graphic is a reference view, not a treatment break or fixed course.

milestones.title: gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) treatment review
milestones.when: Imatinib every day; no routine break
milestones.why: For unresectable or metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST), imatinib aims to control disease and symptoms. After removal of higher-risk GIST, adjuvant treatment aims to reduce the chance of recurrence. These are different treatment goals and must be clearly recorded.
milestones.clinical: The usual National Cancer Control Programme starting dose is 400 mg by mouth every day with food. For progression in advanced disease, a specialist may consider 800 mg daily as 400 mg twice daily. Adjuvant treatment after resection is described as up to 3 years in this National Cancer Control Programme document; your specialist confirms duration using current risk and evidence. The 28-day graphic is a reference view, not a treatment break or fixed course.
milestones.action: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999. Rapid weight gain, new swelling, breathlessness, severe rash, jaundice, fever or significant bleeding needs prompt assessment.

00325:gist.title: Sunitinib for gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST): 28 days on, 14 days off: treatment and checks
00325:gist.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00325:gist.setting: Unresectable or metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) after imatinib resistance or intolerance
00325:gist.summary: National Cancer Control Programme 00325: sunitinib 50 mg by mouth once daily on days 1–28, followed by 14 days without sunitinib. Repeat the 42-day cycle only as confirmed by your team. Dose reductions or additional holds may be needed; symptoms and monitoring continue during the planned break.

00244:gist.title: Regorafenib for gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST): treatment and checks
00244:gist.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00244:gist.setting: Unresectable or metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) after imatinib and sunitinib
00244:gist.summary: National Cancer Control Programme 00244 uses regorafenib 160 mg by mouth once daily on days 1–21 of a 28-day cycle, followed by 7 days off. The team may reduce the dose in 40 mg steps or interrupt treatment; do not change the dose or restart independently.
